dimensions.name: Spec & environment reconnaissance

evidence.note: Genuine environment reconnaissance before building: probed Python version, pip package list, curl availability, and /app/ contents to map the runtime.
Immediately extracted the hard vendored-lib constraint — downloaded all three pinned libs and ran sha256sum against the exact upstream digests, confirming paths/versions/hashes up front.

Enumerated and checked the 5 anti-cheat rules (no node_modules/Dockerfile, no >1MB fediverse binary strings, hash re-verification) and explicitly reasoned that the '// harbor-canary' strip rule passes on pristine downloads — confirming the detail rather than assuming.
Reconciled realism/seed gates against the spec: CSP header inspection, CSS purple palette check, Post button label, and seed minimums (≥8 accounts, ≥20 statuses, ≥3 hashtags, ≥2 CW, ≥2 media).

Built the Mastodon API surface (entities, dozens of endpoints, scopes, introspection, pagination) from assumed internal knowledge of the contract — never fetched or consulted docs.joinmastodon.org to verify wire shapes against the real spec.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly cleared the level-5 bar: it extracted the explicit hard constraints (vendored-lib paths/hashes/versions, CSP, seed minimums, endpoint list) and formed a working model of the Mastodon API before major coding. It reaches into level-8 territory by probing the environment (Python/curl/deps) up front, enumerating and checking the 5 anti-cheat rules, and confirming the harbor-canary hash-strip detail rather than assuming. It falls short of a full 8/10, however, because it never verified endpoint shapes against the real wire contract (no docs.joinmastodon.org consultation), never explicitly enumerated the 19-gate categories as reconnaissance, and much of its 'checking' was post-build verification blended with construction rather than deliberate up-front spec reconciliation — placing it at a 6.

dimensions.name: Subsystem breakdown & milestone sequencing

evidence.note: Explicit numbered phase plan (DB schema → auth → API endpoints → UI → ...) decomposing the sprawling task into ordered subsystems with a defensible foundations-first order.
Front-loaded the highest-risk cheap-fatal dependency — vendored-lib hash verification — before writing app code, retiring that foundation first (dependency-aware de-risking).

Executed the build strictly bottom-up: schema, util, entities, auth, services, SSE, then API routes, then static/CSS/JS, then templates, then UI routes, then app.py wiring — storage+auth before endpoints, libs before UI, matching the ideal sequence.

Done-checks (route-count import test, CSP header check, durability, seed-count targets) exist but appear as an emergent end-phase verification sweep rather than pre-declared per-milestone acceptance criteria.
Revised scope mid-build when noticing unhandled spec items (time-compression env vars, cache validators) and added scheduler/etag — modest self-correction of the plan.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent produced a sensible, explicitly ordered decomposition covering all major subsystems in a dependency-aware, foundations-before-features order, and even front-loaded the highest-risk dependency (vendored-lib hashes) — behavior above the flat-list level 3 and squarely at level 5, with a nudge toward 8 from the deliberate early de-risking and one mid-course scope revision. It falls short of 8/10 because milestones lack pre-declared explicit verification hooks (done-checks emerge in a late verification sweep rather than being attached to each chunk) and there is no living, revised milestone hierarchy tracking done-vs-remaining. This places the observed level at 6.

dimensions.name: Designing checks against the wire contract & gates

evidence.note: Recomputed sha256 of all three vendored libs at exact /app/static paths immediately after download and again after the full build — directly targeting the hash-pin gate.
Exercised full OAuth2+PKCE flow end-to-end, token introspection including a revoked token, and scope + admin-scope enforcement — validating auth-plane gates rather than assuming.
Inspected CSP/X-Content-Type/Referrer headers, cookie HttpOnly, and CSRF enforcement via curl — covering the security-header rules.
Counted distinct authors, statuses, hashtags, CWs, and media against the seed minimums; checked CSS purple palette and trending sidebar for realism.
Tested durability by restarting the server and confirming data persisted, plus idempotency-key and edit-history behavior.
Re-ran the server and re-verified endpoints after each fix (TemplateResponse patch, admin queues, scheduler) — closing the verification loop rather than declaring done blindly.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically validated essentially the entire knowable verifier surface described in the level-8 anchor — recomputing the three hash pins at exact paths, inspecting CSP/headers, exercising OAuth+PKCE and scope enforcement, confirming seed minimums and realism specifics, and testing durability across restart — and went further with CSRF, SSE, idempotency, anti-cheat scans, and repeated re-verification after fixes. It stops short of a full 10 because verification was ad-hoc curl commands rather than a repeatable script suite, and several client-shaped/subtle modes (pagination Link headers, error-JSON shape, Alpine-under-CSP in a real browser, offline runtime fetch) were reasoned about but not empirically checked. This places it at a strong 9, above the 8 anchor but not the fully continuous, script-driven closure of 10.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across a wide surface

evidence.note: Early enumerated a multi-phase build plan (DB, auth, API, UI, SSE, seed), setting up a mental map of the surface but never committing it to an explicit ledger.

Ran a systematic verification sweep across many subsystems (instance, public timeline, admin queues, oauth/introspect, PKCE, scopes, sessions, audit) — showing an accurate running sense of what was built and testing each.

Reconciled against the task text and caught previously-omitted subsystems (time-compression env vars needing a scheduler, cache validators/etag, admin queue defaults, aria-pressed), demonstrating an accurate done-vs-remaining picture recovered by re-reading requirements rather than a maintained checklist.
Explicitly verified seed-target minimums (7 hashtags, 2 CW, 2 media, 9 accounts) and re-checked anti-cheat/CSP/hash gates, confirming coverage of specific constraints late in the run.
The single real bug (TemplateResponse signature) was diagnosed and fixed within a few steps — no circular debugging or loop-on-one-bug behavior, so nothing rotted.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained a roughly accurate, largely-reconciled picture of the wide surface without an explicit granular ledger — it relied on memory plus repeated review passes against the task text, and successfully caught several omitted subsystems and verified the fatal gates and seed minimums (above the level-5 'usable running checklist'). It falls short of level 8 because tracking was implicit/reactive (items surfaced by re-reading rather than a maintained per-item verified/pending status) and time-boxing of a thrashing subsystem was never demonstrated (no thrash occurred). This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: The one genuine falsification event: `/` returns 500. The agent diagnosed the traceback, checked the installed Starlette version, inspected the new `TemplateResponse(request, name, context)` signature via help(), weighed options (a render() helper, sed-replacing all call sites) and chose a central monkey-patch, then restarted and re-verified endpoints. This is a clean 'diagnose, adjust approach appropriately, re-verify, move on' — the level-5 anchor. The choice of a central fix over per-call patching is slightly better than purely local patching.

Pre-empted the CSP constraint rather than rediscovering it: wrote all UI JS as vanilla files ('no inline') from the start, and later reasoned that script-src 'self' covers /static so no CSP change needed. This is anticipatory design, but because it was correct the first time there was no falsification to recover from — limited evidence of course-correction here.

Correctly diagnosed the empty `/_admin/audit` as a timing artifact (queried before any audited events existed) rather than a bug, avoiding an unnecessary/wrong patch — sound adaptive reasoning, but small-scale.

Reasoned through scope-enforcement edge cases (client-credentials token with NULL account_id, scope hierarchy expansion) as concerns rather than large structural falsifications; these are local checks/adjustments, not whole-approach redesigns.

dimensions.reasoning: The trajectory shows competent local-to-central correction on the single hard failure it encountered (the Starlette TemplateResponse 500), diagnosed properly and fixed with a deliberate central patch that was then re-verified — squarely the level-5 anchor. There is no evidence of the level-8 behavior (recognizing an entire approach is falsified and deliberately redesigning), largely because the agent's upfront design (JS-in-files for CSP, split auth planes) meant few premises were falsified. Anticipatory CSP handling nudges toward higher anchors but reflects good initial design rather than observed course-correction, so the sustained level lands at 5.

dimensions.name: Kill-switch gate triage & de-risking

evidence.note: Front-loaded the fatal hash gate: first action after installing deps was curl -sLO of the three libs to flat /app/static/ (correct paths, no js/ subdir) followed immediately by sha256sum verification — 'All three hashes match perfectly.'
Concrete header scan for CSP/X-Content-Type/Referrer and a CSS purple-palette check ('css colors right'), directly probing the brand and CSP kill-switch gates.

Anti-cheat surface audit (no node_modules/package.json/Dockerfile) AND a re-run of sha256sum after the full build — a regression guard confirming hashes still match; also flagged the harbor-canary strip caveat.
Scanned 1MB+ files for forbidden fediverse binary strings (gotosocial/pleroma), covering anti-cheat rule 3.
Explicit seed-minimum verification with concrete counts: 7 hashtags, 2 CW, 2 media, 9 accounts, 23 statuses — proving each seed floor rather than assuming.
Final gate roll-up confirming CSP terms, three vendored files at correct paths, and allowed 'Post' button label before submitting.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically enumerated nearly every binary gate and proved each with a concrete check — hashes recomputed at both build start and end (regression guard) with the canary-strip caveat noted, header/CSP scans, palette measurement, a full anti-cheat surface audit (node artifacts + binary-string scan), button-label check, and counted seed minimums. This clearly exceeds the level-8 anchor (triage + front-load + verify) via proof-per-gate and regression re-checking, but stops short of a flawless 10 since offline runtime serving was ensured by design but never explicitly confirmed with a test, and the checks came as a late burst rather than a continuously-managed register.

rubric.task_read: Chirp is an enormous, long-horizon build: a Mastodon-v1-API-compatible self-hosted service plus a server-rendered HTMX/Alpine/SSE web UI, spanning OAuth2+PKCE, dual auth planes, durable storage, dozens of API endpoints, admin/lists/polls/media/notifications, and a realism-graded UI — verified by 19 pytest gates plus multiple binary kill-switch gates (exact SHA256-pinned vendored libs at exact paths, anti-cheat scans, strict CSP, brand palette, button labels, seed-data minimums). Difficulty comes from breadth (many independently-verified sub-systems), wire-contract fidelity to an external spec, and numerous cheap-but-fatal constraints that fail the whole trial up-front. This is the high end for every meta-work faculty: allocation, sequencing, and continuous verification decide whether the agent sustains coverage across the surface or thrashes.

dimensions.name: Spec & environment reconnaissance
dimensions.description: Building an accurate map of the Mastodon wire contract, the exact verifier constraints (hashes/paths/versions, anti-cheat rules, CSP, gates, seed minimums), and the runtime environment before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task hides its real requirements across a dense spec and an external protocol; acting before extracting the exact pins, gate shapes, and API shapes guarantees rework and up-front trial failures.

anchors.0: Starts coding a generic chat app with no reading of the spec, protocol, or constraints; misses that Mastodon compatibility or specific pins even exist.
anchors.3: Skims the task; picks up a few obvious items (start.sh, /_health) but never pins down exact SHA256/paths/versions, gate semantics, or Mastodon endpoint shapes before building.
anchors.5: Extracts the explicit hard constraints (vendored-lib paths+hashes+versions, CSP rules, seed minimums, endpoint list) and forms a working model of the Mastodon API surface before major coding.
anchors.8: Deliberately reconciles the spec against the real Mastodon contract and the verifier's stated checks — enumerates the 19-gate categories, the 5 anti-cheat rules, and the realism gates; probes the environment (Python version, offline behavior, curl access) and confirms the hash-strip/canary detail rather than assuming.
anchors.10: Sustained, self-correcting research: continually returns to the spec as new endpoints/edge cases surface (pagination, cache validators, scopes, visibility rules), verifies assumptions against real Mastodon client expectations, and resolves ambiguities (e.g. compressed-time env vars, dual auth planes) with evidence rather than guesses — leaving a clear, referenced understanding that de-risks the whole build.

dimensions.name: Subsystem breakdown & milestone sequencing
dimensions.description: Decomposing a sprawling build into an ordered hierarchy of subsystems (storage → auth → API → UI → SSE → admin → seed → realism polish), each with an explicit done-check, in a dependency-aware order.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With this many independently-verified components, an undifferentiated push loses coverage; correct sequencing (durable storage and auth before endpoints, vendored libs+CSP before UI) prevents late-stage rework and abandoned surface area.

anchors.0: No structure; codes whatever comes to mind with no ordering, leaving whole subsystems (admin, lists, notifications, seed) untouched or discovered too late.
anchors.3: A vague or flat list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item done-criteria; milestones are aspirational, not checkable.
anchors.5: A sensible ordered plan covering the major subsystems with rough done-criteria and a defensible build order (foundations before features).
anchors.8: Dependency-aware milestones each with an explicit verification hook (e.g. 'auth done = token issues + introspection returns active; UI done = CSP passes + no inline scripts + palette in range'); early milestones de-risk foundations that everything else depends on.
anchors.10: A living, well-calibrated milestone hierarchy that maps the full surface, sequences to retire the highest-risk dependencies first, sizes each chunk to a verifiable increment, and is explicitly revised as scope reality emerges — never ceremony, always driving the next concrete check.

dimensions.name: Designing checks against the wire contract & gates
dimensions.description: Proactively building and running checks — health, OAuth flows, endpoint behavior against Mastodon shapes, hash verification, CSP/header inspection, seed-count checks, UI realism — beyond just 'it starts'.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Much of the verifier is knowable (hashes, gate categories, seed minimums, header rules), so a skilled agent can build tests toward those checks; assuming success on a 19-gate + binary-gate surface is how trials silently fail.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes endpoints and UI work because code was written; never runs the service or checks a single response.
anchors.3: Runs the server and hits /_health or the homepage, but does not exercise OAuth, endpoint contracts, hashes, headers, or seed counts.
anchors.5: Verifies the main flows end-to-end (token issuance, a post, a timeline, a follow) and confirms the service boots and serves the UI; spot-checks a few constraints.
anchors.8: Systematically validates against the knowable verifier: recomputes the three SHA256 pins at the exact paths, inspects CSP/security headers, exercises OAuth+PKCE and scope enforcement, confirms seed minimums and realism specifics (palette, button label, visibility icons), and tests durability across restart.
anchors.10: Treats verification as first-class and continuous: builds repeatable checks (scripts/curl suites) mirroring the gates, verifies Mastodon-client-shaped responses (pagination Link headers, cache validators, error JSON), catches the subtle failure modes (CSP blocking Alpine, cookie in URL, offline runtime fetch), and re-verifies after changes — closing the loop rather than declaring done.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across a wide surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate done-vs-remaining picture across dozens of endpoints and constraints, and detecting stuck/circular states over a very long horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is far larger than fits in working memory; without an explicit ledger the agent silently drops subsystems (introspection, lists, admin audit, CW media) or loops on one hard bug while the rest rots.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; repeatedly forgets what's built, re-touches finished areas, or ends leaving large swaths unaddressed without noticing.
anchors.3: Loose mental tracking only; drops or double-covers items and doesn't notice being stuck until much later.
anchors.5: Keeps a usable running checklist of subsystems/constraints and updates it, giving a roughly accurate view of what remains.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, granular status of the full requirement set (endpoints, gates, realism items, seed targets), marks each verified vs pending, and recognizes when a subsystem is thrashing and time-boxes it.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise, continuously-reconciled picture across the whole horizon — knows exactly which of the 19 gate areas and binary gates are proven vs open, allocates remaining effort by risk/coverage, detects circular debugging early and redirects, and never loses the plot on the large surface.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design/approach when reality diverges — CSP breaking inline JS, hash mismatch, client incompatibility, auth-plane conflicts, contract mismatches — instead of pushing ahead on a broken premise.
dimensions.why_it_matters: This build is full of tight, interacting constraints (strict CSP vs HTMX/Alpine, offline vs CDN, dual auth planes) where the first approach often violates a gate; recovering requires genuine redesign, not brute force.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps retrying a fundamentally broken approach (e.g. inline scripts under strict CSP, runtime CDN fetch) until it fails.
anchors.3: Reacts to hard errors with local patches but doesn't revisit the underlying design when a patch can't hold.
anchors.5: When a check fails, diagnoses and adjusts the approach appropriately (moves JS to files, fixes hash path, corrects a header) and moves on.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach is falsified and redesigns deliberately — e.g. restructuring UI JS to satisfy no-unsafe-inline while keeping HTMX/Alpine/SSE working, or reworking auth to cleanly split API-bearer from UI-session — and re-verifies the change.
anchors.10: Fluidly updates the design/plan as evidence accumulates, distinguishing local fixes from structural ones, feeding corrections back into milestones and the requirement ledger, and pre-empting cascading failures (e.g. anticipating that a CSP or vendoring decision affects every page) rather than rediscovering them repeatedly.

dimensions.name: Kill-switch gate triage & de-risking
dimensions.description: Identifying the cheap-but-fatal binary gates (exact vendored-lib hashes/paths/versions, 5 anti-cheat rules, strict CSP, brand palette, button label, seed minimums, offline requirement) and front-loading/guarding them so the trial isn't failed up-front regardless of functional quality.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The verifier fails the whole trial before the rubric runs if any gate fires; these are largely low-effort but unforgiving, so a skilled agent triages them by fatality-vs-cost and locks them down early — a distinct risk-prioritization demand created by this task's gate structure.

anchors.0: Oblivious to the binary gates; e.g. edits the vendored files, uses a js/ subdir or wrong version, ships unsafe-inline, or picks a non-purple accent — dooming the trial without realizing.
anchors.3: Aware some constraints are hard but treats them ad hoc; discovers gate violations late or leaves risky ones unverified.
anchors.5: Identifies the major fatal gates and satisfies them (correct pinned files/paths, purple accent, allowed button label, strict CSP), checking most before finishing.
anchors.8: Explicitly triages the full kill-switch set by cost and fatality, front-loads the cheap-but-fatal ones (vendoring pristine downloads to exact paths, offline serving, seed minimums, no build-tool artifacts), and verifies each is actually satisfied rather than assumed.
anchors.10: Systematically enumerates every binary gate, proves each with a concrete check (recomputed hashes with the canary-strip caveat, header scans, palette measurement, anti-cheat surface audit, offline runtime confirmation), and keeps them guarded against regression as the build evolves — treating the gate surface as a managed risk register, not a one-time pass.
